description: Labelled adverse-media corpus. items[]: single-headline classification cases — label 'adverse' = genuinely adverse, must be ACTIONABLE (flagged + eligible for the repeat-escalation counter); 'noise' = weak/generic-keyword headline that must stay flagged-for-the-record but NOT actionable; 'wrong-subject' = adverse story about a different party (low name-token overlap), logged but not actionable; 'clean' = must not flag at all. keywords_in records where the risk terms sit (title/description) — description-only adverse items are the pre-hardening recall gap. engines limits which engine a case scores against (non-Latin headlines are Python-pass cases by design: the JS engine deliberately requires the subject name in the headline). Cross-script relevance rule: a title whose script shares no letters with the subject's script is UNSCORABLE for name-relevance and must be treated as pass-through (counted when its keyword tier passes) — relevance gating must never exclude non-Latin press. repeat_scenarios[]: multi-day evidence-counter simulations against the >=3-stories/90-days signal; day_offset is relative to the runner's fixed reference date.
